findings.F1: The book is long on 84 % of all bars (81 % in w12 to w16), so its falls are mostly the coins' own falls. Its deepest fall is -57.8 % over 480 days from w12 to w16, while holding the coins fell -80.5 % over the same stretch. That gives a Calmar of 0.21 and a Sharpe below holding's.
findings.F2: The rebound after a plunge depends on how violent the coin's last week has been against its last month. The measure is the 7-day to 30-day hourly-volatility ratio at the case bar; 6118 cases over 48 hours.
findings.F3: The book's gain sits almost entirely in high-ratio bars.
findings.F4: Outside w12 to w16 the volatility gradient is steep. Mean excess return rises from -0.17 % to -0.30 %, +0.07 %, +0.84 % (t 3.59) and +1.37 % (t 5.20, n 740) across the ratio fifths, and the Spearman of forecast against outcome rises from 0.01 to 0.10.
findings.F5: Inside w12 to w16 the rebound is absent at every ratio.
findings.F6: Among high-ratio cases (ratio above 1), the rebound grows with the drop: +0.01 %, +0.73 % (t 3.49), +0.42 % and +1.98 % (t 4.22, n 331) across the forecast bands. For the full-size forecast band over all cases it is +0.88 % (n 678).
findings.F7: The past week's move shows the same split. Plunges after the largest 7-day falls rebound +0.75 % (t 2.94), and after the largest 7-day rises +1.02 % (t 3.98). Plunges after middling weeks lose -0.39 % (t -2.15) and -0.28 % (t -1.71). The 30-day return shows the same U shape (+0.55 % and +0.61 % at the ends, -0.58 % at t -3.07 just below zero).
findings.F8: Taken unconditionally, the idea is about the size of one trade's cost.

ideas.idea: When a coin's 24-hour return, read at an hourly close, falls by a large multiple of its 30-day average absolute daily return, the price rises over the next 2 days by more than the coin's usual 2-day drift. The larger the 24-hour drop in those multiples, and the higher the coin's hourly volatility over the past 7 days against its past 30 days, the larger the rise.
ideas.consequence: A trader buys an hourly plunge only in proportion to how turbulent the coin's last week has been against its last month, and stays out of plunges in calm weeks, where the rebound is absent.
ideas.name: plunge rebound in turbulent weeks

ideas.idea: When a coin's 24-hour return, read at an hourly close, falls by a large multiple of its 30-day average absolute daily return, the price rises over the next 2 days by more than the coin's usual 2-day drift. The larger the 24-hour drop in those multiples, and the larger the coin's 7-day return in either direction against its usual 7-day move, the larger the rise.
ideas.consequence: A trader buys a plunge that comes after a week of large moves either way, and does not buy one that interrupts a quiet week.
ideas.name: plunge after an extreme week

ideas.idea: After a coin's 24-hour return falls by a large multiple of its 30-day average absolute daily return, read at an hourly close, the price rises over the next 2 days by more than the coin's usual 2-day drift. The rise is larger the higher the coin's 7-day hourly volatility against its 30-day hourly volatility.
ideas.consequence: A trader takes a 2-day long in a coin only after a plunge in a turbulent week, sized by the turbulence, and is out the rest of the time. This removes most of the drift exposure that carries this book's falls.
ideas.name: turbulence-graded capitulation rebound
